title: Model, data, and prompt decisions
focus: Choose from representative evidence; customize only the responsibility that needs it.

items.decision: Compare supported models using representative held-out inputs, capability/modality, limits, safety, latency, cost, and Region/API support.
items.trap: Public benchmark rank alone is insufficient.

items.decision: Format/examples/tone → prompting and supported structured output. Private/current/attributable knowledge → RAG. Stable behavior still fails evaluated prompts → supported customization.
items.trap: Validate schema AND business meaning. Low temperature is not truth or determinism. RAG and customization can combine; assess data quality, benefit, lifecycle cost, and serving support.

items.decision: Use Knowledge Bases with a supported store; use a supported Lambda transformation for custom chunking. Own query orchestration or retrieval only where the managed contract does not fit.
items.trap: OpenSearch does not automatically mean custom RAG. Custom chunking alone does not force rebuilding ingestion, retrieval, and citations. Extra control adds operations cost.

items.decision: Semantic intent → vector retrieval. Exact IDs → exact lookup, lexical, or supported hybrid. Lost passage context → evaluate chunking/overlap or parent-child retrieval.
items.trap: Preserve searchable identifiers and measure recall. Hybrid is not universally superior. Evaluate chunking/overlap or parent-child retrieval; larger chunks dilute precision/use tokens, semantic chunking is not a universal default, and GraphRAG has a different contract.

items.clue: Data preparation must be a gate
items.decision: Validate extracted structure before database/index writes. Apply and verify required PII redaction; use explicit Glue/Data Quality failure or quarantine rules for invalid records.
items.trap: A report is not a gate; IsComplete alone does not validate non-empty text. Preserve layout and speaker turns, but do not treat speaker labels as verified roles. Fix detached PDF columns before chunking; check native audio support before requiring text conversion.

items.clue: Versioned configuration is not a release gate
items.decision: Prompt Management versions reusable instructions. AppConfig deployment + polling/extension changes application routing. Model/LoRA releases need evaluation → governed artifact/approval → compatible serving/deployment.
items.trap: Versions do not prove quality or approval. AppConfig is not instantaneous global mutation. Registry alone does not update endpoints or hot-swap adapters.

items.decision: Check completed synchronization, ingestion failures, update/delete handling, and derived copies; coalesce/pace StartIngestionJob requests.
items.trap: An S3 update alone does not prove index refresh. Check freshness, entitlement, recall, context budget, and citation support.

title: Execution, integration, and recovery
focus: Choose who controls progress before choosing the runner.

items.decision: One bounded stateless operation → Lambda. Known durable states/retries/approval → Step Functions. Model-selected next tools → bounded agent. Long-lived/custom runtime → suitable ECS/Fargate or agent hosting.
items.trap: Externalize durable state; conventional Lambda invocations are limited to 15 minutes. Persistent processes differ from session state; GPU/host needs require suitable hosting. Complexity alone does not justify orchestration. AgentCore Runtime hosts agents; the implementation or managed harness owns the loop.

items.decision: Agent proposes → validate scope/parameters → durable approval/action workflow where required.
items.trap: The business API still enforces authorization, approval, and idempotency. Bound tool scope, iterations, time, and tokens; a framework does not supply business authorization.

items.decision: SQS → absorb bursts and pace workers. EventBridge → route events to independent targets; add queues where buffering is needed.
items.trap: Queue age, visibility timeout, DLQ, retries, and rate control matter. Shared workers distribute work rather than broadcast it to every consumer. Concurrency alone is not a model token-rate limit.

items.decision: S3 EventBridge delivery → rule → Step Functions. For object bursts, filter keys, buffer, then pace.
items.trap: Direct bucket notifications cannot target a state machine or SQS FIFO.

items.decision: Bedrock Flows → supported typed nodes/branches. Converse/ConverseStream → common supported-model chat API. Keep authoritative state, validate intent/entities, and request missing fields.
items.trap: Flows is not model-selected next-action reasoning. The application supplies relevant message history; an inference call is not a conversation store. InvokeModel can also implement chat with a model-specific contract.

items.decision: Immediate acknowledgement → valid proxy response/direct integration plus tracked job state. WebSocket tokens → decode stream events and send to the connection ID.
items.trap: Async acceptance is not business completion. Storing a connection ID does not resume a model stream.

items.decision: Use application/Lambda code for lightweight normalization/schema checks; versioned infrastructure constructs + runtime wrappers + CI for consistent redaction/logging. Q Developer can assist IDE review/edit/test.
items.trap: Preserve meaningful identifiers/case; Comprehend is not arbitrary query normalization. Review the actual diff and execute tests; avoid obsolete command syntax.

title: Security, governance, and evidence
focus: Identity, access, safety, privacy, and residency are separate controls.

items.decision: Cognito/federation authenticates callers; IAM + application/data authorization limits actions and business data. Roles Anywhere uses trusted CA/X.509 credentials for eligible headless workloads.
items.trap: Authentication and directory integration alone do not establish document/tool permission. Authorize backend scope → ACL/filter → retrieval; the ingestion role does not authorize every caller to every vector.

items.decision: Use supported Guardrails input/output policies and deterministic checks for content risks; enforce tool/data permission separately.
items.trap: Schema compliance is not factual correctness. Retrieved documents/tool results can carry injection; safety filtering does not enforce tenant access. Lake Formation filters do not block independent direct S3 access.

items.decision: S3 discovery → Macie; text pipeline → Comprehend; model I/O → Guardrails.
items.trap: Detection is not verified redaction, and filtered output does not sanitize all logs or derived copies.

items.decision: Interface VPC endpoint/PrivateLink + private DNS + network/endpoint policy/IAM → private role-restricted inference. KMS/TLS/Secrets Manager + least privilege → bytes and secrets.
items.trap: A private subnet alone does not create the private service path. Remove bypasses. Encryption does not establish entitlement, residency, or deletion.

items.decision: SCPs/permissions boundaries limit applicable permissions. Config checks supported resource configuration; GuardDuty detects supported threats; Security Hub aggregates supported findings.
items.trap: Ceilings do not grant access; explicit denies still apply. Config does not inspect every prompt; threat/finding services are not inline content filters or detectors of every GenAI attack.

items.clue: Which evidence answers the audit question?
items.decision: AWS API caller/time/location → CloudTrail with required event coverage. Prompt/response → explicitly enabled, protected Bedrock invocation logging for supported calls.
items.trap: API metadata is not prompt content. Logs can contain sensitive input, including pre-masking input; apply access, encryption, retention, and delivery monitoring.

items.decision: Exactly one approved Region → in-Region inference. Approved geographic destinations → eligible geographic profile. No geographic restriction → evaluate eligible global/geographic profiles.
items.trap: Check EVERY destination: geography labels are insufficient for a permitted subset. Private encrypted transport does not authorize another Region. Source-Region application recovery and retention/deletion of all derived copies remain separate.

title: Cost, latency, and operational efficiency
focus: Identify the repeated work and measure the actual bottleneck.

items.decision: Flexible intermittent traffic → on-demand. Stable measured token demand → evaluate Provisioned Throughput.
items.trap: On-demand still has quotas/throttles. Check hourly billing, sizing, support, and commitment; no universal 60–70% break-even or guaranteed lower p99.

items.decision: Supported offline S3 dataset → Bedrock batch inference. Earlier visible output while waiting → streaming with end-to-end transport.
items.trap: Check job semantics, record reconciliation, model/Region support, and completion objectives. Streaming is not async and need not make generation faster/cheaper; handle buffering, disconnects, and partial failures. Avoid universal batch discount/latency claims.

items.decision: Cross-Region profile → broader eligible compute pool. Intelligent Prompt Routing or custom routing/cascade → simpler queries use less capability.
items.trap: Geographic controls/source-endpoint recovery remain separate. Evaluate both query groups; native routing has model-pair/family restrictions. Custom routing does not inherently need Step Functions.

items.decision: Identical long prefix/questions differ → Bedrock prompt caching. Equivalent questions/valid answer → semantic response cache. Identical complete scoped input/configuration → exact cache/fingerprint.
items.trap: Prompt cache hits still generate; check supported checkpoints, TTL, hits, and billing. Answer caches can skip generation only with a valid entry. Calibrate similarity, scope, freshness, expiry/eviction/invalidation, and unsafe reuse.

items.decision: Changing latency/tokens/throttles/errors/queue age → CloudWatch metrics/alarms. Slow/failed hop → instrumented X-Ray/OTel spans. Across-call prompt/version patterns → Logs Insights over configured logs.
items.trap: Custom quality signals need evaluation/instrumentation. Lambda tracing alone does not expose every SDK call or hidden model stage.

title: Evaluation, diagnosis, and release decisions
focus: Find the first failed boundary; test outcomes before promotion.

items.decision: Missing → inspect ingestion, freshness, source versions, ACLs/filters, query/chunking, and recall. Present but poorly ordered → rerank. Noisy context → evaluate precision, ranking, chunk boundaries, and pruning.
items.trap: Reranking reorders existing candidates and adds latency/cost. Neither reranking nor a larger generator recovers unseen evidence; preserve relevant evidence when pruning.

items.decision: Invented claims → source faithfulness. Off-question answer → answer relevance/task rubric. Fluent wrong action → actual tool selection/parameters, authorization, idempotency, and completion.
items.trap: Citation presence is not source support. Correctness, relevance, and faithfulness differ. Use source-fact/business assertions plus factuality evaluation before promotion.

items.decision: Agent failure → correlated agent trace + tool logs/workflow history. Semantic assessment at scale → calibrated LLM judge. High-risk labels → experts with guidelines/adjudication. Repeatable regressions → assertions/suitable automated metrics.
items.trap: Persist required trace events; memory summaries are different evidence. Judges need rubrics and human calibration/bias checks; humans are fallible. BLEU/ROUGE overlap is not semantic truth or tool correctness.

items.decision: Offline → same held-out cases/sources/rubric. A/B → live outcome comparison with stable cohorts and attribution.
items.trap: Apply prior safety gates and gather enough evidence; no mandatory 50/50 split. Block a release that improves averages but breaks a critical cohort or repeats a business write.

items.decision: Canary → small live cohort + stop/rollback + gradual promotion. Shadow → mirrored requests without candidate responses. Blue/green → switch prepared environments. Synthetic canary → scheduled integration probe.
items.trap: Isolate shadow side effects and account for duplicated data/cost. Validate rollback/state compatibility. Uptime alone does not prove factual quality.
